newsitem.title: INDIA: Pro-India Kashmir chief escapes bomb attack - agency.
newsitem.headline: Pro-India Kashmir chief escapes bomb attack - agency.

text.p: The chief minister of India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state, Farooq Abdullah, narrowly escaped a bomb attack on Thursday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency said the bomb exploded minutes before Abdullah reached his father's grave in the state's summer capital Srinagar to pay homage on his 91st birth anniversary.

It quoted official sources as saying Kashmiri militants detonated the bomb just outside the main gate of the graveyard of Sheikh Abdullah, Kashmir's first chief minister, close to the state's holiest Moslem shrine of Hazratbal.
"No one was hurt but a private taxi was damaged," PTI said.
It said several of Abdullah's cabinet colleagues and other state politicians were present near the site when the explosion rocked the area at 1150 local time (0620 GMT).

Abdullah, leader of the Kashmir's pro-India National Conference party, was named chief minister in October after his party won a sweeping majority in the state's first assembly polls since a violent separatist revolt broke out in 1990.

The explosion came the day after the state leader of the Communist Party of India-Marxist, Yusuf Tarigami, escaped a bomb attack during a political rally in Kulgam town, 65 km (40 miles) south of Srinagar.
Four people were killed and at least 15 injured in Wednesday's attack. Tarigami and one of his bodyguards were slightly injured.
